## Why the first positional rewire is invalid

`Ports.coordinatesFrom` allocates coordinates in declared port and within-port order. It does not sort or use external axis labels. The source of canonical post D33 is one Bits2 owner120 labelled [1,0]; its destination is one Bits2 owner0 labelled [0,1]. Both become the same Layout port `basis=[bits 2], axes=[0,1]`.

`Layout.PortsMatch` requires the complete output basis to equal its selected input basis and `output.axes.map (indexAt layout.axes) = input.axes`. Keeping one complete Bits2 owner and owners=[0], changing only map axes to [1,0] makes this equality [1,0]=[0,1], which is false. The bijection test itself succeeds, but it is insufficient: a rewire cannot permute coordinates inside an intact typed owner. `NodeTyping.conditions` and `ContractTyping.meaningConditions` both retain this full condition; ordinary Rule cannot override it. This is a concrete invalid predicate sufficient to explain structural refusal, without claiming the public output uniquely names its first internal failing predicate.

Actual old reversal D29/M29/P29 is different: it splits owner101 Bits2 at position0 into Bit plus Bits1, puts the selected Bit at position1 into a fresh Bits2 owner, then legally renames labels with a coordinate-identity rewire. `Structural.axisMap` reads the actual take/put interfaces. Its route is [1,0], while its external interface is owner101 Bits2 axes[0,1] on both sides. No implicit coercion or label-based reversal is involved.
